sourceDate.text: 唐乾寧三年至周廣順元年

units.zh: 馬殷，字霸圖，許州鄢陵人也。
units.en: Ma Yin, whose style name was Batu, came from Yanling in Xuzhou.
units.literal: Ma Yin, styled Batu, was a native of Yanling in Xuzhou.

units.zh: 唐中和三年，蔡州秦宗權遣孫儒、劉建峰將兵萬人屬其弟宗衡，略地淮南，殷初為儒裨將。
units.en: In the third year of the Zhonghe reign (883), Qin Zongquan of Caizhou dispatched Sun Ru and Liu Jianfeng with ten thousand men under his younger brother Zongheng to seize territory in Huainan, and Yin began as a junior officer under Sun Ru.
units.literal: In the third year of Zhonghe of Tang, Qin Zongquan of Caizhou sent Sun Ru and Liu Jianfeng leading ten thousand troops under his younger brother Zongheng to raid Huainan; Yin at first served as Ru's deputy commander.

units.zh: 宗衡等攻楊行密於揚州，未克，梁兵方急攻宗權，宗權數召儒等，儒不欲還，宗衡屢趨之，儒怒，殺宗衡，自將其兵取高郵，遂逐行密。
units.en: Zongheng and his forces besieged Yang Xingmi at Yangzhou without success. While Liang armies were tightening their assault on Zongquan, he kept calling Sun Ru back, but Ru refused to return. When Zongheng pressed him repeatedly, Ru in a rage killed Zongheng, took command of the troops himself, captured Gaoyou, and drove Yang Xingmi away.
units.literal: Zongheng and the others attacked Yang Xingmi at Yangzhou but could not take it; Liang troops were pressing hard against Zongquan, who repeatedly summoned Ru and the rest; Ru did not wish to return, and Zongheng urged him again and again; Ru grew angry, killed Zongheng, himself led the army to take Gaoyou, and thus drove off Xingmi.

units.zh: 行密據宣州，儒以兵圍之，久不克，遣殷與建峰掠食旁縣。
units.en: Yang Xingmi held Xuancheng, and Sun Ru laid siege for a long time without breaking the city. He then sent Yin and Liu Jianfeng to raid grain from the surrounding counties.
units.literal: Xingmi held Xuancheng; Ru besieged it with troops for a long time without success, and sent Yin and Jianfeng to forage in neighboring counties.

units.zh: 儒戰敗死，殷等無所歸，乃推建峰為帥，殷為先鋒，轉攻豫章，略虔、吉，有眾數萬。
units.en: When Sun Ru was defeated and killed, Yin and his comrades had nowhere to turn. They made Liu Jianfeng their leader, with Yin as vanguard, swung toward Yuzhang, overran Gan and Ji prefectures, and mustered tens of thousands of men.
units.literal: Ru was defeated and died; Yin and the others had nowhere to go, so they made Jianfeng commander, with Yin as vanguard; they turned to attack Yuzhang, seized Gan and Ji, and had a force of tens of thousands.

units.zh: 乾寧元年，入湖南，次醴陵。
units.en: In the first year of Qianning (894) they marched into Hunan and camped at Liling.
units.literal: In the first year of Qianning, they entered Hunan and halted at Liling.

units.zh: 潭州刺史鄧處訥發邵州兵戍龍回關，建峰等至關，降其戍將蔣勛。
units.en: Deng Chuna, prefect of Tanzhou, sent Shaozhou troops to hold Longhui Pass. When Jianfeng's army arrived, the garrison commander Jiang Xun submitted to them.
units.literal: Tanzhou prefect Deng Chuna dispatched Shaozhou troops to garrison Longhui Pass; when Jianfeng and the others reached the pass, they induced the garrison commander Jiang Xun to surrender.

units.zh: 建峰取勛鎧甲被先鋒兵，張其旗幟，直趨潭州，至東門，東門守者以為關兵戍還，開門內之，遂殺處訥，建峰自稱留後。
units.en: Jianfeng clad his vanguard in Jiang Xun's armor, flew Xun's banners, and marched straight on Tanzhou. At the east gate the guards mistook them for the Longhui garrison coming off rotation and let them in. They killed Deng Chuna, and Jianfeng declared himself acting military governor.
units.literal: Jianfeng took Xun's armor and put it on the vanguard troops, displayed his banners, and rushed straight to Tanzhou; at the east gate the defenders thought the pass garrison was returning from duty and opened the gate to admit them; they then killed Chuna, and Jianfeng styled himself military governor.

units.zh: 僖宗授建峰湖南節度使、殷為馬步軍都指揮使。
units.en: Emperor Xizong appointed Jianfeng military commissioner of Hunan and made Yin overall commander of the horse and foot forces.
units.literal: Emperor Xizong appointed Jianfeng military commissioner of Hunan and Yin commander-in-chief of horse and foot armies.

units.zh: 蔣勛求為邵州刺史，建峰不與，勛率兵攻湘鄉，建峰遣殷擊勛於邵州。
units.en: Jiang Xun sought appointment as prefect of Shaozhou, but Jianfeng refused. Xun then marched on Xiangxiang, and Jianfeng sent Yin to fight him in Shaozhou.
units.literal: Jiang Xun asked to be made prefect of Shaozhou; Jianfeng refused; Xun led troops to attack Xiangxiang; Jianfeng sent Yin to strike Xun at Shaozhou.

units.zh: 建峰庸人，不能帥其下，常與部曲飲酒歡呼。
units.en: Jianfeng was a mediocrity who could not keep discipline among his men and spent his time drinking and carousing with the rank and file.
units.literal: Jianfeng was a mediocre man who could not command his subordinates and often drank and shouted with his troops.

units.zh: 軍卒陳贍妻有色，建峰私之，贍怒，以鐵楇擊殺建峰。
units.en: A soldier named Chen Shan had a beautiful wife whom Jianfeng seduced. Enraged, Shan killed Jianfeng with an iron mace.
units.literal: The soldier Chen Shan's wife was beautiful; Jianfeng took her privately; Shan in anger struck and killed Jianfeng with an iron mace.

units.zh: 軍中推行軍司馬張佶為帥，佶將入府，乘馬輒踶嚙，傷佶髀。
units.en: The troops proposed acting army marshal Zhang Ji as leader. As he was entering headquarters, his mount kicked and bit him, wounding his thigh.
units.literal: The army advanced acting army marshal Zhang Ji as commander; as Ji was about to enter the headquarters, the horse he mounted kicked and bit, injuring Ji's thigh.

units.zh: 佶臥病，語諸將曰：「吾非汝主也，馬公英勇，可共立之。」
units.en: Confined to his sickbed, Ji told the officers, "I am not fit to lead you. Lord Ma is valiant—you should install him together."
units.literal: Ji lay ill and told the generals, "I am not your lord; Lord Ma is brave—together you may establish him."

units.zh: 諸將乃共殺贍，磔其屍，遣姚彥章迎殷於邵州。
units.en: The officers thereupon executed Chen Shan and displayed his body on a rack, then sent Yao Yanzhang to bring Yin back from Shaozhou.
units.literal: The generals then together killed Shan, exposed his corpse on a rack, and sent Yao Yanzhang to welcome Yin at Shaozhou.

units.zh: 殷至，佶乘肩輿入府，殷拜謁於廷中，佶召殷上，乃率將吏下，北面再拜，以位與之，時乾寧三年也。
units.en: When Yin arrived, Zhang Ji was carried into headquarters in a sedan. Yin bowed in the courtyard, and Ji called him up. Ji then led the officers downstairs, faced north, and twice performed the full obeisance before yielding command to Yin. It was the third year of Qianning (896).
units.literal: When Yin arrived, Ji entered the headquarters in a sedan chair; Yin bowed in the courtyard; Ji summoned Yin up; then he led the officers down, bowed twice facing north, and yielded the position to him—it was the third year of Qianning.

units.zh: 唐拜殷潭州刺史。
units.en: The Tang court appointed Yin prefect of Tanzhou.
units.literal: Tang appointed Yin prefect of Tanzhou.

units.zh: 殷遣其將秦彥暉、李瓊等攻連、邵、郴、衡、道、永六州，皆下之。
units.en: Yin sent Qin Yanhui, Li Qiong, and other generals against the six prefectures of Lian, Shao, Chen, Heng, Dao, and Yong, and all fell to him.
units.literal: Yin sent his generals Qin Yanhui, Li Qiong, and others to attack the six prefectures of Lian, Shao, Chen, Heng, Dao, and Yong; all were taken.

units.zh: 桂管劉士政懼，遣其將陳可璠、王建武等率兵守全義嶺。
units.en: Liu Shizheng, commissioner of Guiguan, grew alarmed and sent Chen Kefan, Wang Jianwu, and others to hold Quanyi Ridge with an army.
units.literal: Guiguan commissioner Liu Shizheng was afraid and sent his generals Chen Kefan, Wang Jianwu, and others to lead troops to hold Quanyi Ridge.

units.zh: 殷遣使聘於士政，使者至境上，可璠等不納。
units.en: Yin sent envoys to treat with Liu Shizheng, but when they reached the frontier Chen Kefan and his men refused them entry.
units.literal: Yin sent envoys on a friendly mission to Shizheng; when the envoys reached the border, Kefan and the others would not admit them.

units.zh: 殷怒，遣瓊等以兵七千攻之，擒可璠等及其兵二千餘人，悉坑之，遂圍桂管，虜士政，盡取其屬州。
units.en: Enraged, Yin sent Li Qiong with seven thousand men. They captured Chen Kefan and more than two thousand troops and buried them alive, then besieged Guiguan, took Liu Shizheng captive, and annexed all his dependent prefectures.
units.literal: Yin was angry and sent Qiong and others with seven thousand troops to attack; they captured Kefan and others and more than two thousand of their soldiers, buried them all alive, then besieged Guiguan, took Shizheng prisoner, and seized all his subordinate prefectures.

units.zh: 殷表瓊桂管觀察使。
units.en: Yin recommended Li Qiong to the throne as observation commissioner of Guiguan.
units.literal: Yin memorialized recommending Qiong as Guiguan observation commissioner.

units.zh: 四年，拜殷武安軍節度使。
units.en: In the fourth year Yin was appointed military commissioner of the Wu'an army.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed military commissioner of the Wu'an army.

units.zh: 初，孫儒敗於宣州，殷弟賨為楊行密所執，行密收儒余兵為「黑雲都」，以賨為指揮使。
units.en: After Sun Ru's defeat at Xuancheng, Yin's younger brother Ma Cong fell into Yang Xingmi's hands. Xingmi enrolled Sun Ru's survivors in the "Black Cloud Corps" and appointed Cong its commander.
units.literal: Earlier, when Sun Ru was defeated at Xuancheng, Yin's younger brother Cong was seized by Yang Xingmi; Xingmi took Ru's remaining troops into the "Black Cloud Corps" and made Cong its commander.

units.zh: 賨從行密攻戰，數有功，為人質重，未嘗自矜，行密愛之，問賨誰家子，賨曰：「馬殷弟也。」
units.en: Cong fought under Yang Xingmi with repeated distinction. Steady and never self-aggrandizing, he won Xingmi's affection. When Xingmi asked whose son he was, Cong answered, "I am Ma Yin's younger brother."
units.literal: Cong followed Xingmi in campaigns and repeatedly distinguished himself; he was grave in bearing and never boastful; Xingmi favored him and asked whose son he was; Cong said, "I am Ma Yin's younger brother."

units.zh: 行密大驚曰：「汝兄貴矣，吾今歸汝可乎？」
units.en: Yang Xingmi was astonished. "Your brother has risen high," he said. "Shall I send you back to him now?"
units.literal: Xingmi was greatly startled and said, "Your elder brother is exalted now—shall I return you to him today?"

units.zh: 賨不對。
units.en: Cong made no reply.
units.literal: Cong did not answer.

units.zh: 他日又問之，賨謝曰：「臣，孫儒敗卒也，幸公待以不死，非殺身不足報。
units.en: On another day Xingmi asked again. Cong demurred: "I am only a beaten man from Sun Ru's army. You spared my life; nothing short of dying for you could repay that debt.
units.literal: Another day he asked again; Cong declined and said, "Your servant is a defeated soldier of Sun Ru; by your grace I was spared death—only giving my life would be inadequate repayment.

units.zh: 湖南鄰境，朝夕聞殷動靜足矣，不願去也。」
units.en: Hunan lies next door; hearing news of my brother each day is enough. I do not wish to go."
units.literal: Hunan is a neighboring territory—hearing morning and evening of Yin's movements is enough; I do not wish to leave."

units.zh: 行密嘆曰：「昔吾愛子之貌，今吾得子之心矣。
units.en: Xingmi sighed. "Once I admired your face; now I have won your loyalty.
units.literal: Xingmi sighed and said, "Formerly I loved your appearance; now I have won your heart.

units.zh: 然勉為吾合二國之歡，通商賈、易有無以相資，亦所以報我也！」
units.en: Still, work to keep our two realms on friendly terms, let merchants pass freely, and trade what one has for what the other lacks. That will be your repayment to me as well!"
units.literal: Yet strive to join the goodwill of our two states, open trade, and exchange what each lacks to support the other—that too is how you may repay me!"

units.zh: 乃厚禮遣賨歸。
units.en: He then sent Cong home with rich gifts and full honors.
units.literal: He then sent Cong home with generous gifts.

units.zh: 殷大喜，表賨節度副使。
units.en: Yin was overjoyed and recommended his brother as deputy military commissioner.
units.literal: Yin was greatly pleased and memorialized recommending Cong as deputy military commissioner.

units.zh: 行密遣將劉存等攻杜洪，圍鄂州，殷遣秦彥暉、許德勛以舟兵救之，已而杜洪敗死，存等遂攻殷。
units.en: Yang Xingmi sent Liu Cun and others against Du Hong and besieged Ezhou. Yin dispatched Qin Yanhui and Xu Dexun with a fleet to aid Hong, but Hong soon fell and died, whereupon Liu Cun turned on Yin.
units.literal: Xingmi sent generals Liu Cun and others to attack Du Hong and besieged Ezhou; Yin sent Qin Yanhui and Xu Dexun with river troops to rescue him; before long Du Hong was defeated and died, and Cun and the others then attacked Yin.

units.zh: 殷遣彥暉拒於上流，偏將黃璠以舟三百伏瀏陽口。
units.en: Yin posted Qin Yanhui upstream while his deputy Huang Fan hid three hundred boats at Liuyang Ford.
units.literal: Yin sent Yanhui to hold the upper reaches; deputy commander Huang Fan lay in ambush at Liuyang Ford with three hundred boats.

units.zh: 存等屢戰不勝，乃致書於殷以求和，殷欲許之，彥暉曰：「淮人多詐，將怠我師，不可信。」
units.en: After repeated defeats Liu Cun sued for peace. Yin was inclined to accept, but Yanhui warned, "The Huainan men are treacherous. They mean to lull our troops—do not trust them."
units.literal: Cun and the others repeatedly fought without victory and then sent a letter to Yin seeking peace; Yin wished to agree; Yanhui said, "Huainan men are much given to deceit—they will weary our army; they cannot be trusted."

units.zh: 急擊之，存等退走，黃璠以瀏陽舟截江合擊，大敗之，劉存及陳知新戰死，彥暉取岳州。
units.en: He pressed the attack. Liu Cun withdrew, Huang Fan's Liuyang squadron cut the river and struck from the flank, and the Huainan force was shattered. Liu Cun and Chen Zhixin were killed, and Yanhui seized Yuezhou.
units.literal: He pressed the attack urgently; Cun and the others retreated; Huang Fan with the Liuyang boats blocked the river and joined the strike, inflicting a great defeat; Liu Cun and Chen Zhixin died in battle; Yanhui took Yuezhou.

units.zh: 梁太祖即位，殷遣使修貢，太祖拜殷侍中兼中書令，封楚王。
units.en: After the Liang founder took the throne, Yin sent tribute missions. The emperor made him palace attendant and director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed him as King of Chu.
units.literal: When the Taizu of Liang took the throne, Yin sent envoys to present tribute; the Taizu appointed Yin palace attendant and concurrently director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed him as King of Chu.

units.zh: 荊南高季昌以兵斷漢口，邀殷貢使，殷遣許德勛攻其沙頭，季昌求和，乃止。
units.en: Gao Jichang of Jingnan blocked the Han River crossing and waylaid Yin's tribute bearers. Yin sent Xu Dexun against Jichang's Shatou base; when Jichang sued for peace, the fighting stopped.
units.literal: Gao Jichang of Jingnan used troops to cut the Hankou crossing and intercept Yin's tribute envoys; Yin sent Xu Dexun to attack his Shatou stronghold; Jichang sought peace, and the action ceased.

units.zh: 楊行密袁州刺史呂師周來奔。
units.en: Lü Shizhou, prefect of Yuanzhou under Yang Xingmi, defected to Chu.
units.literal: Lü Shizhou, Yang Xingmi's prefect of Yuanzhou, came to defect.

units.zh: 師周，勇健豪俠，頗通緯候、兵書，自言五世將家，懼不能免，常與酒徒聚飲，醉則起舞，悲歌慷慨泣下。
units.en: Shizhou was bold, dashing, and versed in divination and military classics. Claiming five generations of commanders in his line, he feared he could not escape disaster. He drank with wastrels, and when drunk would dance, sing dirges with fierce emotion, and weep.
units.literal: Shizhou was brave, robust, and chivalrous, well versed in prognostication and military texts; he said himself that for five generations his house had produced generals; he feared he could not escape harm; he often drank with roisterers; when drunk he would dance, sing mournful songs with passionate force, and weep.

units.zh: 行密聞之，疑其有異志，使人察其動靜。
units.en: When Yang Xingmi heard of this, he suspected disloyalty and set spies on Shizhou's conduct.
units.literal: Xingmi heard of this, suspected him of disloyal intent, and sent men to watch his movements.

units.zh: 師周益懼，謂其裨將綦毋章曰：「吾與楚人為敵境，吾常望其營上雲氣甚佳，未易敗也。
units.en: More frightened than ever, Shizhou told his lieutenant Qimu Zhang, "We share a border with Chu. I have watched the clouds over their camps—they look auspicious. They will not be easy to beat.
units.literal: Shizhou grew still more afraid and said to his deputy Qimu Zhang, "We border the Chu people; I have often looked at the clouds above their camp—they are very auspicious; they will not be easy to defeat.

units.zh: 吾聞馬公仁者，待士有禮，吾欲逃死於楚可乎？」
units.en: I hear Lord Ma is humane and treats men of talent with courtesy. Could I save my life by fleeing to Chu?"
units.literal: I have heard that Lord Ma is benevolent and treats scholars with courtesy—might I flee death by going to Chu?"

units.zh: 章曰：「公自圖之，章舌可斷，語不泄也。」
units.en: Zhang replied, "My lord, decide as you will. They may cut out my tongue, but I will never betray you."
units.literal: Zhang said, "My lord, plan for yourself—Zhang's tongue may be cut off, but his words will not leak."

units.zh: 師周以兵獵境上，乃奔於楚，綦毋章縱其家屬隨之。
units.en: Shizhou led a hunting party to the frontier and slipped into Chu. Qimu Zhang allowed his household to follow.
units.literal: Shizhou took troops hunting on the border and then fled to Chu; Qimu Zhang let his family go with him.

units.zh: 殷聞師周至，大喜曰：「吾方南圖嶺表而得此人，足矣。」
units.en: When Yin learned Shizhou had come, he exclaimed with delight, "I was plotting south into Lingnan, and to gain this man is enough."
units.literal: When Yin heard Shizhou had arrived, he was greatly pleased and said, "I was just planning to advance south into Lingnan and have gained this man—that is enough."

units.zh: 以為馬步軍都指揮使，率兵攻嶺南，取昭、賀、梧、蒙、龔、富等州。
units.en: He appointed him commander of horse and foot and sent him into Lingnan, where he captured Zhao, He, Wu, Meng, Gong, Fu, and other prefectures.
units.literal: He made him commander-in-chief of horse and foot, led troops to attack Lingnan, and took the prefectures of Zhao, He, Wu, Meng, Gong, and Fu.

units.zh: 殷表師周昭州刺史。
units.en: Yin recommended Shizhou as prefect of Zhaozhou.
units.literal: Yin memorialized recommending Shizhou as prefect of Zhaozhou.

units.zh: 朗州雷彥恭召吳人攻平江，許德勛擊敗之。
units.en: Lei Yangong of Langzhou called in Wu forces against Pingjiang, but Xu Dexun routed them.
units.literal: Lei Yangong of Langzhou summoned Wu troops to attack Pingjiang; Xu Dexun defeated them.

units.zh: 殷遣秦彥暉攻朗州，彥恭奔於吳，執其弟彥雄等七人送於梁。
units.en: Yin sent Qin Yanhui against Langzhou. Yangong fled to Wu, while Yanhui seized Yangong's brother Yanxiong and six others and sent them to the Liang court.
units.literal: Yin sent Qin Yanhui to attack Langzhou; Yangong fled to Wu; they seized his younger brother Yanxiong and six others and sent them to Liang.

units.zh: 於是澧州向瑰、辰州宋鄴、漵州昌師益等率溪洞諸蠻皆附於殷。
units.en: Then Xiang Gui of Lizhou, Song Ye of Chenzhou, Chang Shiyi of Xuzhou, and other leaders of the stream-dwelling tribes all submitted to Yin.
units.literal: Thereupon Xiang Gui of Lizhou, Song Ye of Chenzhou, Chang Shiyi of Xuzhou, and others leading the various Man of the stream valleys all submitted to Yin.

units.zh: 殷請升朗州為永順軍，表張佶節度使。
units.en: Yin asked that Langzhou be raised to the Yongshun army district and recommended Zhang Ji as its military commissioner.
units.literal: Yin requested that Langzhou be elevated to the Yongshun army and memorialized recommending Zhang Ji as its military commissioner.

units.zh: 殷乃請依唐太宗故事，開天冊府，置官屬。
units.en: Yin then petitioned, citing Emperor Taizong's precedent, to establish a Celestial Registry Office with a full staff.
units.literal: Yin then asked, following the precedent of Emperor Taizong of Tang, to open a Celestial Registry Office and appoint officials.

units.zh: 太祖拜殷天冊上將軍，殷以其弟賨為左相，存為右相，廖光圖等十八人為學士。
units.en: The Liang founder named Yin Celestial-Registry Grand General. Yin made his brothers Ma Cong left chancellor and Ma Cun right chancellor, with Liao Guangtu and seventeen others as academicians.
units.literal: The Taizu appointed Yin Celestial-Registry Grand General; Yin made his younger brothers Ma Cong left chancellor and Ma Cun right chancellor, and Liao Guangtu and seventeen others academicians.

units.zh: 末帝時，加殷武昌、靜江、寧遠等軍節度使，洪、鄂四面行營都統。
units.en: Under the Last Emperor of Liang, Yin was further given the Wuchang, Jingjiang, and Ningyuan commands and made overall commander of the Hong-E mobile headquarters.
units.literal: In the time of the Last Emperor he added to Yin the military commissions of the Wuchang, Jingjiang, and Ningyuan armies, and overall command of the Hong-E region mobile camp.

units.zh: 唐莊宗滅梁，殷遣其子希範修貢京師，上梁所授都統印。
units.en: After Tang Zhuangzong overthrew Liang, Yin sent his son Ma Xifan to court with tribute and returned the overall-command seal the Liang had bestowed.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong of Tang destroyed Liang, Yin sent his son Xifan to present tribute at the capital and surrendered the overall-command seal granted by Liang.

units.zh: 莊宗問洞庭廣狹，希範對曰：「車駕南巡，才堪飲馬爾。」
units.en: Zhuangzong asked how vast Dongting Lake was. Xifan answered, "If Your Majesty's carriage came south on tour, the lake would scarcely hold enough water for your horses to drink."
units.literal: Zhuangzong asked how wide and narrow Dongting Lake was; Xifan replied, "If Your Majesty's carriage toured south, it would barely suffice to water the horses."

units.zh: 莊宗嘉之。
units.en: The emperor was pleased.
units.literal: Zhuangzong praised this.

units.zh: 莊宗平蜀，殷大懼，表求致仕，莊宗下璽書慰勞之。
units.en: When Zhuangzong conquered Shu, Yin was terrified and asked to retire. Zhuangzong sent a sealed letter of reassurance.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Shu, Yin was greatly afraid and memorialized requesting retirement; Zhuangzong issued an imperial letter of consolation and encouragement.

units.zh: 明宗即位，遣使修貢，並賀明年正月，荊南高季昌執其貢使史光憲。
units.en: When Mingzong succeeded, Yin sent tribute and New Year's greetings, but Gao Jichang of Jingnan seized the envoy Shi Guangxian.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Yin sent envoys to present tribute and also to congratulate the coming first month of the new year; Gao Jichang of Jingnan seized his tribute envoy Shi Guangxian.

units.zh: 殷遣袁詮、王環等攻之，至其城下，季昌求和，乃止。
units.en: Yin sent Yuan Quan, Wang Huan, and others against Jingnan. They reached the city walls, Jichang sued for peace, and the attack ended.
units.literal: Yin sent Yuan Quan, Wang Huan, and others to attack; they reached the foot of his walls; Jichang sought peace, and the campaign stopped.

units.zh: 殷初兵力尚寡，與楊行密、成汭、劉龑等為敵國，殷患之，問策於其將高郁，郁曰：「成汭地狹兵寡，不足為吾患，而劉龑志在五管而已，楊行密，孫儒之仇，雖以萬金交之，不能得其歡心。
units.en: Early on Yin's forces were still weak, and he faced Yang Xingmi, Cheng Jun, and Liu Yan as enemies. Troubled, he asked his general Gao Yu for counsel. Yu said, "Cheng Jun has little land and few troops—not a real threat. Liu Yan cares only for the Five Guan. Yang Xingmi, Sun Ru's foe, will never be won with gold, however much you spend.
units.literal: At first Yin's military strength was still slight; he was at enmity with Yang Xingmi, Cheng Jun, Liu Yan, and others; Yin was troubled and asked strategy of his general Gao Yu; Yu said, "Cheng Jun's territory is narrow and his troops few—he is not enough to be our worry; Liu Yan's ambition is only the Five Guan; Yang Xingmi is Sun Ru's enemy—even with ten thousand in gold in friendship you cannot win his heart.

units.zh: 然尊王仗順，霸者之業也，今宜內奉朝廷以求封爵而外誇鄰敵，然後退修兵農，畜力而有待爾。」
units.en: Yet hegemony rests on honoring the throne and claiming the moral high ground. Serve the court inwardly for titles, overawe your neighbors outwardly, then husband troops and fields, store strength, and wait."
units.literal: Yet honoring the king and relying on legitimacy is the work of a hegemon; now you should inwardly serve the court to seek enfeoffment and titles while outwardly overawing neighboring enemies; then withdraw to train troops and cultivate agriculture, store strength, and wait."

units.zh: 於是殷始修貢京師，然歲貢不過所產茶茗而已。
units.en: Yin then began sending tribute to the capital, though each year's offering was only the tea his domain produced.
units.literal: Thereupon Yin began presenting tribute to the capital, yet the annual tribute was no more than the tea produced in his domain.

units.zh: 乃自京師至襄、唐、郢、復等州置邸務以賣茶，其利十倍。
units.en: He set up tea agencies from the capital through Xiang, Tang, Ying, Fu, and other prefectures, reaping ten times the profit.
units.literal: He then from the capital to Xiang, Tang, Ying, Fu, and other prefectures established lodge offices to sell tea, with profits tenfold.

units.zh: 郁又諷殷鑄鉛鐵錢，以十當銅錢一。
units.en: Yu also persuaded Yin to mint lead-iron coins valued at ten for one standard copper cash.
units.literal: Yu also urged Yin to cast lead-iron coin, ten pieces counting as one copper cash.

units.zh: 又令民自造茶以通商旅，而收其算，歲入萬計。
units.en: He let the people produce tea for trade and taxed it, yielding tens of thousands in annual revenue.
units.literal: He also ordered the people to make tea themselves to facilitate merchants and travelers, while collecting excise; annual receipts ran to tens of thousands.

units.zh: 由是地大力完，數邀封爵。
units.en: His domain grew rich and powerful, and he repeatedly petitioned for higher titles.
units.literal: By this the territory grew strong and resources complete, and he repeatedly sought enfeoffment.

units.zh: 天成二年，請建行臺。
units.en: In the second year of Tiancheng (927), he petitioned to establish a traveling office.
units.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng, he requested the establishment of a traveling office.

units.zh: 明宗封殷楚國王，有司言無封國王禮，請如三公用竹冊，乃遣尚書右丞李序持節以竹冊封之。
units.en: Mingzong enfeoffed Yin as King of Chu. The responsible offices said no rite existed for enfeoffing a territorial king and asked that the Three Dukes' bamboo-register ceremony be followed. Mingzong then sent Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Xu with credentials and a bamboo register to invest him.
units.literal: Mingzong enfeoffed Yin as King of Chu; the responsible offices said there was no rite for enfeoffing a king of state, and asked that it follow the bamboo registers used for the Three Dukes; he then sent Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Xu bearing credentials with a bamboo register to invest him.

units.zh: 殷以潭州為長沙府，建國承制，自置官屬，以其弟賨為靜江軍節度使，子希振武順軍節度使，次子希聲判內外諸軍事，姚彥章為左相，許德勳為右相，李鐸為司徒，崔穎為司空，拓拔常為僕射，馬珙為尚書，文武皆進位。
units.en: Yin made Tanzhou the capital as Changsha Prefecture, declared a state, and assumed imperial authority. He appointed his own officials: younger brother Cong as Jingjiang commissioner; son Xizhen as Wushun commissioner; second son Xisheng to oversee military affairs; Yao Yanzhang as left chancellor and Xu Dexun as right chancellor; Li Duo as Minister of Education, Cui Ying as Minister of Works, Tuoba Chang as Vice Director, and Ma Gong as Director of the Secretariat. Civil and military officials all received promotions.
units.literal: Yin made Tanzhou into Changsha Prefecture, established a state and assumed imperial authority, and appointed his own officials: his younger brother Cong military commissioner of the Jingjiang Army; his son Xizhen military commissioner of the Wushun Army; his second son Xisheng to judge internal and external military affairs; Yao Yanzhang as left chancellor; Xu Dexun as right chancellor; Li Duo as Minister of Education; Cui Ying as Minister of Works; Tuoba Chang as Vice Director; Ma Gong as Director of the Secretariat; civil and military officials all advanced in rank.

units.zh: 謚其曾祖筠曰文肅、祖正曰莊穆、父元豐曰景莊，立三廟于長沙。
units.en: He posthumously titled his great-grandfather Jun Wensu, his grandfather Zheng Zhuangmu, and his father Yuanfeng Jingzhuang, and built three ancestral temples at Changsha.
units.literal: He gave posthumous titles to his great-grandfather Jun as Wensu, his grandfather Zheng as Zhuangmu, and his father Yuanfeng as Jingzhuang, and established three ancestral temples at Changsha.

units.zh: 長興元年，殷卒，年七十九，詔曰「馬殷官爵俱高，無以為贈，謚曰武穆」而已。
units.en: In the first year of Changxing (930), Yin died at seventy-nine. The court issued only this edict: "Ma Yin's offices and titles are already so exalted that no further gifts can be granted; his posthumous title is Wumu."
units.literal: In the first year of Changxing, Yin died at seventy-nine. An edict said only: "Ma Yin's offices and titles are already so high that nothing more can be granted in gift; his posthumous title shall be Wumu."

units.zh: 子希聲立。
units.en: His son Xisheng succeeded him.
units.literal: His son Xisheng succeeded.

units.zh: 希聲字若訥，殷次子也。
units.en: Xisheng, styled Ruone, was Yin's second son.
units.literal: Xisheng, styled Ruone, was Yin's second son.

units.zh: 殷建國，以希聲判內外諸軍事。
units.en: When Yin founded the state, he put Xisheng in charge of military affairs.
units.literal: When Yin established the state, he made Xisheng judge internal and external military affairs.

units.zh: 荊南高季昌聞殷將高郁素教殷以計策而楚以彊，患之，嘗使諜者行間於殷，殷不聽。
units.en: Gao Jichang of Jingnan heard that Yin's general Gao Yu had long advised him with stratagems that made Chu strong and was alarmed. He once sent agents to sow discord, but Yin paid no heed.
units.literal: Gao Jichang of Jingnan heard that Yin's general Gao Yu had long taught Yin stratagems by which Chu grew strong, and was troubled by it; he once sent spies to sow discord with Yin, but Yin would not listen.

units.zh: 希聲用事，諜者語希聲曰：「季昌聞楚用高郁，大喜，以為亡馬氏者必郁也。」
units.en: Once Xisheng held power, a spy told him: "Jichang heard Chu employs Gao Yu and rejoiced, convinced Yu would destroy the Ma clan."
units.literal: When Xisheng held power, a spy told Xisheng: "Jichang heard that Chu employs Gao Yu and rejoiced greatly, thinking that the one who will destroy the Ma clan must be Yu."

units.zh: 希聲素愚，以為然，遽奪郁兵職，郁怒曰：「吾事君王久矣，亟營西山，將老焉，犬子漸大，能咋人矣！」
units.en: Xisheng was naturally dull and believed it. He abruptly stripped Yu of his command. Yu raged: "I have served my lord for years. I was building a retreat on West Mountain to grow old, and my pup is growing teeth!"
units.literal: Xisheng was naturally foolish and believed it; he abruptly stripped Yu of his military post. Yu in anger said: "I have served my lord long. I was just building my retreat on West Mountain to grow old there, and my pup is growing up and can bite people!"

units.zh: 希聲聞之，矯殷令殺郁。
units.en: Hearing this, Xisheng forged an order in Yin's name and had Yu killed.
units.literal: When Xisheng heard this, he forged an order from Yin and had Yu killed.

units.zh: 殷老不復省事，莫知郁死，是日大霧四塞，殷怪之，語左右曰：「吾嘗從孫儒，儒每殺不辜，天必大霧，豈馬步獄有冤死乎？」
units.en: Yin was old and no longer managed affairs and did not know Yu was dead. That day fog closed in on every side. Yin found it strange and told his attendants: "When I followed Sun Ru, every wrongful killing brought thick fog. Are there innocent men dying in the cavalry and infantry prisons?"
units.literal: Yin was old and no longer attended to affairs; he did not know Yu had died. That day dense fog closed in on all sides. Yin thought it strange and said to those at his side: "When I followed Sun Ru, Ru whenever killed the innocent heaven always sent great fog. Could there be wrongful deaths in the cavalry and infantry prisons?"

units.zh: 明日，吏以狀白，殷拊膺大哭曰：「吾荒耄如此，而殺吾勳舊！」
units.en: The next day an official reported what had happened. Yin beat his breast and wept: "I have grown so feeble, yet I killed a meritorious old companion!"
units.literal: The next day an official reported the facts. Yin beat his breast and wept loudly, saying: "I am so senile, and yet I killed my meritorious old companion!"

units.zh: 顧左右曰：「吾亦不久於此矣！」
units.en: He told his attendants: "I shall not remain here much longer!"
units.literal: He turned to those at his side and said: "I shall not remain here much longer!"

units.zh: 明年殷薨。
units.en: The following year Yin died.
units.literal: The next year Yin died.

units.zh: 希聲立，授武安、靜江等軍節度使。
units.en: When Xisheng succeeded, he received the Wu'an, Jingjiang, and related military commissions.
units.literal: Xisheng succeeded; he was appointed military commissioner of the Wu'an, Jingjiang, and other armies.

units.zh: 希聲嘗聞梁太祖好食雞，慕之，乃日烹五十雞以供膳。
units.en: Hearing that Liang's founder loved chicken, Xisheng imitated him and had fifty birds cooked every day for his table.
units.literal: Xisheng had heard that the Taizu of Liang loved to eat chicken and admired this, so he daily cooked fifty chickens for his meals.

units.zh: 葬殷上潢，希聲不哭泣，頓食雞肉數器而起。
units.en: At Yin's burial at Shanghuang, Xisheng did not weep but devoured several platters of chicken and then stood up.
units.literal: When Yin was buried at Shanghuang, Xisheng did not weep but bolted down several platters of chicken and then rose.

units.zh: 其禮部侍郎潘起譏之曰：「昔阮籍居喪而食蒸豚，世豈乏賢邪！」
units.en: His vice minister of rites Pan Qi mocked him: "When Ruan Ji ate steamed pork in mourning, people said the age lacked worthy men—and here we are again!"
units.literal: His vice minister of rites Pan Qi mocked him, saying, "In old days Ruan Ji during mourning ate steamed pork—is the age short of worthy men!"

units.zh: 長興三年，希聲卒，追封衡陽王。
units.en: In the third year of Changxing (932) he died and was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Hengyang.
units.literal: In the third year of Changxing, Xisheng died and was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Hengyang.

units.zh: 弟希範立。
units.en: His younger brother Ma Xifan succeeded him.
units.literal: His younger brother Xifan succeeded.

units.zh: 希範字寶規，殷第四子也。
units.en: Ma Xifan, styled Baogui, was Yin's fourth son.
units.literal: Xifan, styled Baogui, was Yin's fourth son.

units.zh: 殷子十餘人，嫡子希振長而賢，其次希聲與希範同日生，而希聲母袁夫人有美色，希聲以母寵得立，而希振棄官為道士，居於家。
units.en: Yin had more than a dozen sons. The legitimate heir Xizhen was eldest and capable. Xisheng and Xifan were born the same day, but because Xisheng's mother, Lady Yuan, was beautiful, he won the throne through her favor, while Xizhen resigned his posts, became a Daoist, and lived at home.
units.literal: Yin had more than ten sons; the legitimate son Xizhen was eldest and worthy; next Xisheng and Xifan were born the same day; Xisheng's mother Lady Yuan was beautiful; Xisheng through his mother's favor gained succession; Xizhen abandoned office to become a Daoist priest and lived at home.

units.zh: 希聲卒，而希範以次立，襲殷官爵，封楚王。
units.en: After Xisheng's death, Xifan succeeded in birth order, took over Yin's offices and titles, and was enfeoffed as King of Chu.
units.literal: When Xisheng died, Xifan succeeded in order of birth, inherited Yin's offices and titles, and was enfeoffed as King of Chu.

units.zh: 清泰二年，賜以弓矢冠劍。
units.en: In the second year of Qingtai (935) the court bestowed on him the bow, arrows, cap, and sword of investiture.
units.literal: In the second year of Qingtai he was granted bow, arrows, cap, and sword.

units.zh: 天福四年，加希範天冊上將軍，開府承制如殷故事。
units.en: In the fourth year of Tianfu (939) he was named Celestial-Registry Grand General and allowed to open a government with imperial commission, following his father's precedent.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Tianfu he added to Xifan the title Celestial-Registry Grand General and opened a government office with imperial commission, as in Yin's precedent.

units.zh: 希範好學，善詩，文士廖光圖、徐仲雅、李臯、拓拔常等十八人皆故殷時學士，希範性奢侈，光圖等皆薄徒，飲博歡呼，獨常沈厚長者，上書切諫，光圖等惡之。
units.en: Xifan loved learning and wrote poetry well. Eighteen scholars including Liao Guangtu, Xu Zhongya, Li Gao, and Tuoba Chang had served as academicians under Yin. Xifan was extravagant; most of them were idle roisterers who drank and gambled. Only Tuoba Chang, a sober elder, sent a blunt memorial of remonstrance, which the others resented.
units.literal: Xifan loved learning and was skilled in poetry; the literati Liao Guangtu, Xu Zhongya, Li Gao, Tuoba Chang, and eighteen others had all been academicians in Yin's time; Xifan was by nature extravagant; Guangtu and the rest were shallow fellows who drank, gambled, and shouted; only Chang was grave and mature; he submitted a memorial of stern remonstrance; Guangtu and the others hated him.

units.zh: 襄州安從進、安州李金全叛，晉高祖詔希範出兵。
units.en: When An Congjin of Xiangzhou and Li Jinquan of Anzhou rebelled, Jin Gaozu ordered Xifan to march.
units.literal: An Congjin of Xiangzhou and Li Jinquan of Anzhou rebelled; the Gaozu of Jin ordered Xifan to send troops.

units.zh: 希範遣張少敵以舟兵趨漢陽，漕米五萬斛以饋軍，金全等敗，少敵乃旋。
units.en: Xifan sent Zhang Shaodi with a fleet to Hanyang and shipped fifty thousand hu of grain to the imperial army. After the rebels were crushed, Shaodi withdrew.
units.literal: Xifan sent Zhang Shaodi with river troops to hurry to Hanyang and transported fifty thousand hu of grain to supply the army; when Jinquan and the others were defeated, Shaodi then returned.

units.zh: 溪州刺史彭士愁率錦、獎諸蠻攻澧州，希範遣劉勍、劉全明等以步卒五千擊之，士愁大敗。
units.en: Peng Shichou, prefect of Xizhou, led the Jin and Jiang tribes against Lizhou. Xifan sent Liu Qing, Liu Quanming, and five thousand infantry against him, and Shichou was routed.
units.literal: Peng Shichou, prefect of Xizhou, led the Man of Jin and Jiang to attack Lizhou; Xifan sent Liu Qing, Liu Quanming, and others with five thousand foot soldiers to strike them; Shichou was greatly defeated.

units.zh: 勍等攻溪州，士愁走獎州，遣其子師暠率諸蠻酋降於勍。
units.en: Liu Qing and the others pressed the attack on Xizhou. Shichou fled to Jiangzhou and sent his son Shigao with the tribal chiefs to surrender to Liu Qing.
units.literal: Liu Qing and the others attacked Xizhou; Shichou fled to Jiangzhou; he sent his son Shigao leading the various Man chiefs to surrender to Liu Qing.

units.zh: 溪州西接牂柯、兩林，南通桂林、象郡，希範乃立銅柱以為表，命學士李臯銘之。
units.en: Xizhou bordered Zangke and Lianglin on the west and Guilin and Xiang commandery on the south. Xifan set up a bronze pillar as a boundary marker and had the academician Li Gao inscribe it.
units.literal: Xizhou on the west adjoins Zangke and Lianglin; on the south it connects to Guilin and Xiang commandery; Xifan then erected a bronze pillar as a marker and ordered the academician Li Gao to inscribe it.

units.zh: 於是，南寧州酋長莫彥殊率其本部十八州、都雲酋長尹懷昌率其昆明等十二部、牂柯張萬浚率其夷、播等七州皆附於希範。
units.en: Then Mo Yanshu of Nanning led eighteen prefectures, Yin Huaichang of Duyun led twelve Kunming divisions, and Zhang Wanxun of Zangke led seven Yi and Bo prefectures—all submitted to Xifan.
units.literal: Thereupon the chieftain of Nanningzhou Mo Yanshu led his original eighteen prefectures; the chieftain of Duyun Yin Huaichang led his twelve divisions including Kunming; Zhang Wanxun of Zangke led his seven prefectures of Yi and Bo—all submitted to Xifan.

units.zh: 希範作會春園、嘉宴堂，其費巨萬，始加賦於國中，拓拔常切諫以為不可。
units.en: Xifan built the Huichun Garden and Jiayan Hall at enormous cost and raised taxes throughout the realm. Tuoba Chang protested sharply that he should not.
units.literal: Xifan built the Huichun Garden and the Jiayan Hall; the cost was in the tens of thousands; he first increased levies within the state; Tuoba Chang sternly remonstrated that this should not be done.

units.zh: 希範又作九龍殿，以八龍繞柱，自言身一龍也。
units.en: He also built the Hall of Nine Dragons, with eight dragons coiled around the pillars, declaring himself the ninth dragon.
units.literal: Xifan also built the Hall of Nine Dragons, with eight dragons coiling the pillars; he said himself that he was the ninth dragon.

units.zh: 是時，契丹滅晉，中國大亂，希範牙將丁思覲廷諫希範曰：「先王起卒伍，以攻戰而得此州，倚朝廷以制鄰敵，傳國三世，有地數千里，養兵十萬人。
units.en: While the Khitans destroyed Jin and the Central Plains fell into chaos, guardsman Ding Siguan admonished Xifan in open court: "Your grandfather rose from the ranks and won this realm by the sword. He leaned on the throne to hold off neighbors. Three generations have ruled thousands of li and kept a hundred thousand men under arms.
units.literal: At this time the Khitan destroyed Jin and central China was in great disorder; Xifan's guardsman Ding Siguan remonstrated at court, saying, "The former king rose from the ranks, gained this territory by attack and battle, relied on the court to control neighboring enemies, transmitted the state through three generations, holds land of several thousand li, and maintains a hundred thousand troops.

units.zh: 今天子囚辱，中國無主，真霸者立功之時。
units.en: The emperor is captive and the realm has no master. This is the moment for a true hegemon to act.
units.literal: Now the Son of Heaven is imprisoned and shamed; central China has no lord—it is truly the time for a hegemon to establish achievement.

units.zh: 誠能悉國之兵出荊、襄以趨京師，倡義於天下，此桓文、之業也。
units.en: If you marched every soldier through Jing and Xiang toward the capital and rallied the empire, you could match the achievements of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin.
units.literal: If you can truly deploy all the state's troops out through Jing and Xiang to hurry to the capital, raise righteousness under Heaven—this is the achievement of Duke Huan and Duke Wen.

units.zh: 奈何耗國用而窮土木，為兒女之樂乎？」
units.en: Why waste the treasury on palaces and gardens for mere personal pleasure?"
units.literal: Why drain the state's resources and exhaust yourself in construction, for the pleasures of women and children?"

units.zh: 希範謝之，思覲瞋目視希範曰：「孺子終不可教也！」
units.en: Xifan thanked him politely. Siguan glared and said, "This boy will never learn!"
units.literal: Xifan thanked him; Siguan glared at Xifan and said, "This child in the end cannot be taught!"

units.zh: 乃扼喉而死。
units.en: He throttled himself on the spot.
units.literal: He then seized his own throat and died.

units.zh: 開運四年，希範卒，年四十九，謚曰文昭。
units.en: In the fourth year of Kaiyun (947) Xifan died at forty-nine. His posthumous title was Wenzhao, "Cultured and Illustrious."
units.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyun, Xifan died at age forty-nine; his posthumous title was Wenzhao.

units.zh: 希廣立。
units.en: Ma Xiguang succeeded him.
units.literal: Xiguang succeeded.

units.zh: 希廣字德丕，希範同母弟也。
units.en: Ma Xiguang, styled Depi, was Xifan's younger brother by the same mother.
units.literal: Xiguang, styled Depi, was Xifan's younger brother by the same mother.

units.zh: 希範平生惡拓拔常諫諍，常入謁，希範呼閽者指常曰：「吾不欲見此人，勿復內也。」
units.en: Xifan had always disliked Tuoba Chang's blunt counsel. When Chang came to court, Xifan told the gatekeeper, pointing at him, "I do not want to see this man again. Keep him out."
units.literal: Throughout his life Xifan hated Tuoba Chang's remonstrances; when Chang came to audience, Xifan called the gatekeeper, pointed at Chang, and said, "I do not wish to see this man—do not admit him again."

units.zh: 乃謝絕之。
units.en: He shut Chang out entirely.
units.literal: He then declined him with thanks.

units.zh: 及臥病，始思常言，以為忠，召之托以希廣。
units.en: When he fell gravely ill, he recalled Chang's counsel, judged it loyal, summoned him, and entrusted Ma Xiguang to his care.
units.literal: When he fell ill, he then reflected on Chang's words, deemed them loyal, summoned him, and entrusted Xiguang to him.

units.zh: 希範卒，常數勸希廣以位奉其兄希萼，希廣不從。
units.en: After Xifan's death, Chang repeatedly urged Xiguang to yield the throne to his elder brother Ma Xie, but Xiguang refused.
units.literal: When Xifan died, Chang repeatedly urged Xiguang to yield the position to his elder brother Xie, but Xiguang would not comply.

units.zh: 希萼為朗州節度使，希範之卒，希萼自朗州來奔喪。
units.en: Ma Xie held Langzhou as military commissioner. When Xifan died, Xie came from Langzhou to mourn.
units.literal: Xie was military commissioner of Langzhou; when Xifan died, Xie came from Langzhou to attend the funeral.

units.zh: 希廣將劉彥瑫謀曰：「武陵之來，其意不善，宜出兵迎之，以備非常，使其解甲釋兵而後入。」
units.en: Xiguang's general Liu Yantang advised, "Xie's arrival from Wuling bodes ill. Meet him with troops, guard against surprise, and make him disarm before he enters the city."
units.literal: Xiguang's general Liu Yantang plotted, saying, "The man from Wuling comes with ill intent; troops should be sent to meet him against the unexpected, and he should be made to lay aside armor and weapons before entering."

units.zh: 張少敵、周廷誨曰：「王能與之則已，不然宜早除之。」
units.en: Zhang Shaodi and Zhou Tinghui said, "If you can share power, do so; otherwise eliminate him at once."
units.literal: Zhang Shaodi and Zhou Tinghui said, "If Your Majesty can share power with him, so be it; otherwise he should be removed early."

units.zh: 希廣泣曰：「吾兄也，焉忍殺之，分國而治可也。」
units.en: Xiguang wept. "He is my brother. I cannot kill him. Let us divide the realm and rule separately."
units.literal: Xiguang wept and said, "He is my elder brother—how could I bear to kill him? Let us divide the state and each rule a part."

units.zh: 乃以兵迎希萼於砆石，止之於碧湘宮，厚賂以遣之。
units.en: He met Xie with troops at Fushi, lodged him at the Bixiang Palace, lavished gifts on him, and sent him home.
units.literal: He then sent troops to welcome Xie at Fushi, detained him at the Bixiang Palace, and sent him away with rich gifts.

units.zh: 希萼憤然而去，乃遣使詣京師求封爵，請置邸稱藩。
units.en: Xie left in a fury and sent envoys to court seeking titles, a liaison office, and recognition as a vassal state.
units.literal: Xie departed in anger and then sent envoys to the capital seeking enfeoffment, requesting a residence office and status as a vassal.

units.zh: 漢隱帝不許，降璽書慰勞講解之。
units.en: Emperor Yin of Later Han refused but sent a sealed letter of reassurance seeking reconciliation.
units.literal: The Hidden Emperor of Han did not consent but issued an imperial letter of consolation and mediation.

units.zh: 希萼怒，送款於李景，舉兵攻長沙。
units.en: Enraged, Xie pledged allegiance to Li Jing of Southern Tang and marched on Changsha.
units.literal: Xie was angry, submitted allegiance to Li Jing, and raised troops to attack Changsha.

units.zh: 希廣遣劉彥瑫、許可瓊等禦之。
units.en: Xiguang sent Liu Yantang, Xu Keqiong, and others to oppose him.
units.literal: Xiguang sent Liu Yantang, Xu Keqiong, and others to resist him.

units.zh: 彥瑫敗希萼於僕射洲。
units.en: Yantang defeated Xie at Pushe Islet.
units.literal: Yantang defeated Xie at Pushe Islet.

units.zh: 希萼去，誘溪洞諸蠻寇益陽。
units.en: Xie withdrew and stirred the stream-dwelling tribes to raid Yiyang.
units.literal: Xie withdrew and incited the various Man of the stream valleys to raid Yiyang.

units.zh: 希廣遣崔珙璉以步卒七千屯湘鄉玉潭以遏諸蠻。
units.en: Xiguang posted Cui Gonglian with seven thousand infantry at Yutan in Xiangxiang to block the tribal raids.
units.literal: Xiguang sent Cui Gonglian with seven thousand foot soldiers to encamp at Yutan in Xiangxiang to check the various Man.

units.zh: 劉彥瑫以舟兵趨武陵，攻希萼。
units.en: Liu Yantang sailed upriver toward Wuling to strike at Xie.
units.literal: Liu Yantang with river troops hurried to Wuling to attack Xie.

units.zh: 彥瑫敗於湄洲，希廣大懼，遣使請兵於京師，漢隱帝不能出師。
units.en: Yantang was beaten at Meizhou. Terrified, Xiguang begged the court for reinforcements, but Emperor Yin could send none.
units.literal: Yantang was defeated at Meizhou; Xiguang was greatly afraid and sent envoys to request troops from the capital; the Hidden Emperor of Han could not dispatch an army.

units.zh: 希萼舟兵沿江而上，自號「順天將軍」，攻岳州，刺史王赟堅城不戰，希萼呼赟曰：「吾昔約君同行，今何異心乎？」
units.en: Xie's fleet moved upriver under the title "General Who Follows Heaven" and besieged Yuezhou. Prefect Wang Yun held the walls and refused battle. Xie shouted, "We once agreed to march together—why have you turned against me?"
units.literal: Xie's river troops advanced up the river, styled himself "General Who Follows Heaven," attacked Yuezhou; the prefect Wang Yun held the walls firm and would not fight; Xie called to Yun, saying, "I once agreed with you to go together—why a change of heart now?"

units.zh: 赟曰：「君王兄弟不相容，而責將吏異心乎？
units.en: Yun replied, "When royal brothers cannot coexist, how can you blame a servant for choosing sides?
units.literal: Yun said, "The royal brothers cannot tolerate each other—yet you blame a subordinate officer for disloyalty?

units.zh: 願君王入長沙，不傷同氣，臣不敢不盡節。」
units.en: Enter Changsha without harming your brother, and I will serve you to the utmost."
units.literal: I wish Your Majesty to enter Changsha without harming your own kin; your servant dares not fail in duty."

units.zh: 希萼引兵去，下湘鄉，止長沙，屯水西。
units.en: Xie withdrew, moved through Xiangxiang, halted at Changsha, and camped on the west bank of the river.
units.literal: Xie led his troops away, descended on Xiangxiang, halted at Changsha, and encamped west of the water.

units.zh: 劉彥瑫、許可瓊屯水東。
units.en: Liu Yantang and Xu Keqiong held the east bank.
units.literal: Liu Yantang and Xu Keqiong encamped east of the water.

units.zh: 彭師暠登城望水西軍，入白希廣曰：「武陵兵驕，雜以蠻蜑，其勢易破。
units.en: Peng Shigao surveyed the western army from the wall and told Xiguang, "Wuling's troops are arrogant and mixed with tribal auxiliaries—they can be broken easily.
units.literal: Peng Shigao climbed the wall to view the army west of the water, entered to report to Xiguang, saying, "The Wuling troops are arrogant, mixed with Man and Dan boat people—their force is easy to break.

units.zh: 請令可瓊等陣山前，臣以步兵三千自巴溪渡江趨嶽麓，候夜擊之。」
units.en: Post Keqiong's men on the hills in front. I will take three thousand infantry across the river at Baxi Ford toward Yuelu and attack by night."
units.literal: I ask that Keqiong and the others form battle lines before the hills; your servant will take three thousand foot soldiers from Baxi ford the river toward Yuelu and strike when night falls."

units.zh: 希廣以為可，而可瓊已陰送款於希萼，遂沮其議。
units.en: Xiguang agreed, but Keqiong had already secretly defected to Xie, and the plan was shelved.
units.literal: Xiguang thought it feasible, but Keqiong had secretly submitted to Xie, and so the plan was blocked.

units.zh: 明日，師暠詣可瓊計事，瞋目叱之曰：「視汝反文在面，豈欲投賊乎！」
units.en: The next day Shigao came to consult Keqiong, glared, and shouted, "Treason is written on your face—are you going over to the enemy?!"
units.literal: The next day Shigao went to Keqiong to discuss plans, glared at him, and shouted, "I see the word for 'rebel' written on your face—do you mean to join the enemy!"

units.zh: 拂衣而出，急白希廣，請殺之，希廣不聽。
units.en: He stormed out, rushed to Xiguang, and urged Keqiong's execution, but Xiguang refused.
units.literal: He flung his robe and left, urgently reported to Xiguang, and asked to have him killed; Xiguang would not listen.

units.zh: 希萼攻長樂門，牙將吳宏、楊滌戰於門中，希萼少衄，已而許可瓊奔於希萼，宏、滌聞之皆潰。
units.en: Xie assaulted the Changle Gate. Guardsmen Wu Hong and Yang Di fought inside the gate and briefly checked him, but when Xu Keqiong defected to Xie, Hong and Di's forces melted away.
units.literal: Xie attacked the Changle Gate; guardsmen Wu Hong and Yang Di fought within the gate; Xie suffered a slight setback; before long Xu Keqiong fled to Xie; when Hong and Di heard of it they both collapsed.

units.zh: 希廣率妻子匿於慈堂。
units.en: Xiguang hid his wife and children in the Cici Hall.
units.literal: Xiguang led his wife and children to hide in the Cici Hall.

units.zh: 明日擒之。
units.en: The next day they seized him.
units.literal: The next day they captured him.

units.zh: 希萼見之惻然曰：「此鈍夫也，豈能為惡？
units.en: Seeing him, Xie said with pity, "This fool could never have meant harm.
units.literal: When Xie saw him he said with pity, "This is a dull fellow—how could he do evil?

units.zh: 左右惑之爾。」
units.en: His advisers misled him, that is all."
units.literal: It was only those at his side who misled him."

units.zh: 顧其下曰：「吾欲活之，如何？」
units.en: He asked his men, "I want to spare him. What do you say?"
units.literal: He turned to his followers and said, "I wish to spare his life—what say you?"

units.zh: 其下皆不對，遂縊死之。
units.en: No one answered, and Xie had him strangled.
units.literal: His followers all made no reply, and he then strangled him to death.

units.zh: 乾祐三年，希萼自立。
units.en: In the third year of Qianyou (950), Xie declared himself ruler.
units.literal: In the third year of Qianyou, Xie declared himself ruler.

units.zh: 明年，漢隱帝崩，京師大亂，希萼遂臣於李景，景冊封希萼楚王，希萼悉以軍政事任其弟希崇。
units.en: The next year Emperor Yin of Han died and the capital plunged into chaos. Xie then submitted to Li Jing, who enfeoffed him as King of Chu. Xie entrusted all military and civil affairs to his younger brother Xichong.
units.literal: The next year the Hidden Emperor of Han died and the capital fell into great disorder. Xie then submitted to Li Jing; Jing invested Xie as King of Chu, and Xie entrusted all military and civil affairs to his younger brother Xichong.

units.zh: 希崇與楚舊將徐威、陸孟俊、魯綰等謀作亂。
units.en: Xichong plotted rebellion with former Chu officers Xu Wei, Lu Mengjun, Lu Wan, and others.
units.literal: Xichong plotted a revolt with former Chu generals Xu Wei, Lu Mengjun, Lu Wan, and others.

units.zh: 希萼置酒端陽門，希崇辭以疾，威等縱惡馬十餘匹，以壯士執檛隨之，突入其府，劫庫兵，縛希萼，迎希崇以立。
units.en: Xie held a feast at Duanyang Gate. Xichong pleaded illness. Wei and the others turned loose more than ten vicious horses with armed men following, burst into the residence, seized the armory, bound Xie, and installed Xichong.
units.literal: Xie set out wine at the Duanyang Gate. Xichong excused himself on grounds of illness. Wei and the others loosed more than ten vicious horses, with stalwart men wielding maces following them; they burst into the residence, seized the armory weapons, bound Xie, and installed Xichong.

units.zh: 希崇遣彭師暠、廖偃囚希萼於衡山，師暠奉希萼為衡山王，臣於李景。
units.en: Xichong sent Peng Shigao and Liao Yan to imprison Xie at Hengshan. Shigao set Xie up as King of Hengshan under Li Jing.
units.literal: Xichong sent Peng Shigao and Liao Yan to imprison Xie at Hengshan. Shigao installed Xie as King of Hengshan, subject to Li Jing.

units.zh: 希崇懼，亦請命於景。
units.en: Afraid, Xichong also sought orders from Jing.
units.literal: Xichong was afraid and also sought orders from Jing.

units.zh: 景遣邊鎬入楚，盡遷馬氏之族于金陵，時周廣順元年也。
units.en: Jing sent Bian Hao into Chu and moved the entire Ma clan to Jinling. It was the first year of Guangshun (951).
units.literal: Jing sent Bian Hao into Chu and relocated the entire Ma clan to Jinling; it was the first year of Guangshun of Zhou.

units.zh: 封希萼楚王，居洪州；
units.en: He enfeoffed Xie as King of Chu at Hongzhou;
units.literal: He enfeoffed Xie as King of Chu and had him reside at Hongzhou;

units.zh: 希崇領舒州節度使，居揚州。
units.en: Xichong became military commissioner of Shuzhou at Yangzhou.
units.literal: Xichong held the military commission of Shuzhou and resided at Yangzhou.

units.zh: 顯德三年，世宗征淮，下揚州，下詔撫安馬氏子孫。
units.en: In the third year of Xiande (956), Emperor Shizong campaigned in the Huai region, captured Yangzhou, and issued an edict to reassure the Ma clan's descendants.
units.literal: In the third year of Xiande, Shizong campaigned in Huai, took Yangzhou, and issued an edict to comfort and reassure the descendants of the Ma clan.

units.zh: 已而揚州復入於景，希崇率其兄弟十七人歸京師，拜右羽林統軍，希能左屯衛大將軍，希貫右千牛衛大將軍，希隱、希浚、希知、希朗皆為節度行軍司馬。
units.en: Soon Yangzhou returned to Southern Tang control. Xichong led seventeen brothers to the capital. He became commander of the Right Imperial Guard; Xineng, grand general of the Left Palace Guard; Xiguan, grand general of the Right Imperial Bull Lancers; and Xiyin, Xijun, Xizhi, and Xilang received staff appointments under various military commissioners.
units.literal: Before long Yangzhou again fell to Jing; Xichong led his seventeen brothers back to the capital; he was appointed commander of the Right Feathered Forest; Xineng was made grand general of the Left Palace Guard; Xiguan was made grand general of the Right Imperial Bull Lancers; Xiyin, Xijun, Xizhi, and Xilang were all made mobile-camp staff officers of military commissioners.

units.zh: 劉言，吉州廬陵人也。
units.en: Liu Yan came from Luling in Jizhou.
units.literal: Liu Yan was a native of Luling in Jizhou.

units.zh: 王進逵，武陵人也。
units.en: Wang Jinkui was a native of Wuling.
units.literal: Wang Jinkui was a native of Wuling.

units.zh: 言，初事刺史彭玕，從玕奔楚，言事希範為長州刺史。
units.en: Yan had first served Prefect Peng Yan and followed him into Chu. Under Xifan he became prefect of Changzhou.
units.literal: Yan at first served the prefect Peng Yan; he followed Yan in flight to Chu; Yan served Xifan as prefect of Changzhou.

units.zh: 進逵少為靜江軍卒，事希萼為指揮使。
units.en: Jinkui had been a soldier in the Jingjiang army and served Xie as a commander.
units.literal: Jinkui in youth was a soldier of the Jingjiang army and served Xie as a commander.

units.zh: 希萼攻希廣，以進逵為先鋒，陷長沙。
units.en: In Xie's assault on Xiguang, Jinkui led the vanguard and captured Changsha.
units.literal: When Xie attacked Xiguang, he made Jinkui vanguard and took Changsha.

units.zh: 長沙遭亂殘毀，希萼使進逵以靜江兵營緝之，兵皆愁怨，進逵因擁之，夜以長柯巨斧斫關，奔歸武陵。
units.en: Changsha lay in ruins after the fighting. Xie sent Jinkui with Jingjiang troops to restore order, but the men were bitter. Jinkui rallied them, and by night they smashed the gates with long poles and great axes and fled back to Wuling.
units.literal: Changsha had been ravaged by disorder; Xie had Jinkui use Jingjiang troops to camp and restore order; the soldiers were all resentful; Jinkui therefore rallied them; by night with long poles and great axes they hewed through the gate and fled back to Wuling.

units.zh: 希萼方醉，不能省，明日遣將唐翥追之，及於武陵，翥戰大敗而還。
units.en: Xie was too drunk to grasp what had happened. The next day he sent Tang Zhu in pursuit. Zhu caught them at Wuling, was routed, and retreated.
units.literal: Xie was drunk and could not take notice; the next day he sent the general Tang Zhu in pursuit; Zhu caught up at Wuling, fought, was greatly defeated, and returned.

units.zh: 進逵乃逐出留後馬光惠，迎言於辰州以為帥，進逵自為副。
units.en: Jinkui expelled acting governor Ma Guanghui, brought Liu Yan from Chenzhou to lead them, and served as his deputy.
units.literal: Jinkui then drove out the acting governor Ma Guanghui, welcomed Yan from Chenzhou to be commander, and made himself deputy.

units.zh: 已而希萼將徐威等作亂，縛希萼而立希崇，湖南大亂。
units.en: Soon Xie's officer Xu Wei mutinied, bound Xie, and installed Xichong. Hunan plunged into chaos.
units.literal: Before long Xie's general Xu Wei and others made a disturbance, bound Xie, and installed Xichong; Hunan fell into great disorder.

units.zh: 李景遣邊鎬入楚，遷馬氏於金陵，因並召言。
units.en: Li Jing sent Bian Hao into Chu, moved the Ma clan to Jinling, and summoned Liu Yan as well.
units.literal: Li Jing sent Bian Hao into Chu, relocated the Ma clan to Jinling, and thereby also summoned Yan.

units.zh: 言不從，遣進逵與行軍司馬何景真等攻鎬於長沙，鎬敗走。
units.en: Yan refused and sent Jinkui with staff officer He Jingzhen and others against Bian Hao at Changsha. Hao was beaten and fled.
units.literal: Yan would not comply and sent Jinkui with acting army marshal He Jingzhen and others to attack Hao at Changsha; Hao was defeated and fled.

units.zh: 周廣順三年，言奉表京師，以邀封爵。
units.en: In the third year of Guangshun (953), Yan memorialized the Zhou court seeking titles.
units.literal: In the third year of Guangshun of Zhou, Yan presented a memorial to the capital to seek enfeoffment.

units.zh: 又言長沙殘破，不可居，請移治所於武陵。
units.en: He argued that ruined Changsha was uninhabitable and asked to move the capital to Wuling.
units.literal: He also said Changsha was ruined and uninhabitable and requested that the seat of government be moved to Wuling.

units.zh: 周太祖皆從之，乃升朗州為武平軍，在武安軍上，以言為節度使，因以武安授進逵，進逵自以言己所迎立，不為之下。
units.en: Zhou Taizu agreed. Langzhou was raised to the Wuping army, senior to Wu'an. Yan became its military commissioner and Jinkui received Wu'an. Jinkui, having installed Yan himself, refused to bow to him.
units.literal: The Taizu of Zhou granted all of this; Langzhou was then elevated to the Wuping army, ranking above the Wu'an army; Yan was made its military commissioner; the Wu'an command was given to Jinkui; Jinkui considered that Yan was someone he himself had installed and would not serve beneath him.

units.zh: 言患之，二人始有隙，欲相圖。
units.en: Yan grew uneasy. The two men fell out and plotted against each other.
units.literal: Yan was troubled by this; the two men first developed a rift and wished to destroy each other.

units.zh: 進逵謀曰：「言將可用者不過何景真、朱全琇爾，召而殺之，言可取也。」
units.en: Jinkui schemed: "Yan's only capable officers are He Jingzhen and Zhu Quanxiu. Summon and kill them, and Yan is yours."
units.literal: Jinkui plotted, saying, "Among Yan's usable generals there are only He Jingzhen and Zhu Quanxiu—summon and kill them, and Yan can be taken."

units.zh: 是時，劉晟取楚梧、桂、宜、蒙等州，進逵因白言召景真等會兵攻晟。
units.en: Southern Han's Liu Sheng had seized Wu, Gui, Yi, Meng, and other Chu prefectures. Jinkui urged Yan to summon Jingzhen and the rest for a joint campaign against him.
units.literal: At this time Liu Sheng of Southern Han took Wu, Gui, Yi, Meng, and other prefectures of Chu; Jinkui therefore reported to Yan to summon Jingzhen and the others to join forces and attack Sheng.

units.zh: 言信之，遣景真、全琇往，至皆見殺，乃舉兵襲武陵，執言殺之，奉表京師，周太祖即以進逵為武平軍節度使。
units.en: Yan believed him and sent them out. Both were killed on arrival. Jinkui then struck Wuling, seized and executed Yan, and memorialized the court. Zhou Taizu at once appointed Jinkui military commissioner of Wuping.
units.literal: Yan believed him and sent Jingzhen and Quanxiu; when they arrived they were all killed; he then raised troops, surprised Wuling, seized Yan and killed him, and presented a memorial to the capital; the Taizu of Zhou immediately made Jinkui military commissioner of the Wuping army.

units.zh: 世宗征淮南，授進逵南面行營都統。
units.en: When Shizong campaigned in Huainan, he named Jinkui overall commander of the southern expeditionary headquarters.
units.literal: When Shizong campaigned in Huainan, he appointed Jinkui overall commander of the southern mobile headquarters.

units.zh: 進逵攻鄂州，過岳州，岳州刺史潘叔嗣，進逵故時同列，待進逵甚謹。
units.en: Marching on Ezhou, Jinkui passed through Yuezhou, where Prefect Pan Shusi, once his comrade in arms, received him with scrupulous courtesy.
units.literal: Jinkui attacked Ezhou and passed Yuezhou; the prefect of Yuezhou Pan Shusi had been Jinkui's former comrade in rank and received Jinkui with great courtesy.

units.zh: 進逵左右就叔嗣求賂，叔嗣不與，左右讒其短，進逵面罵之，叔嗣慚恨，語其下曰：「進逵戰勝而還，吾無遺類矣。」
units.en: Jinkui's men demanded bribes; Shusi refused. They slandered him, and Jinkui berated him publicly. Ashamed and furious, Shusi told his officers, "If Jinkui wins and returns, none of us will be left alive."
units.literal: Jinkui's attendants approached Shusi to demand bribes; Shusi would not give them; the attendants slandered his faults; Jinkui reviled him to his face; Shusi was ashamed and resentful and told his men, "If Jinkui returns victorious from battle, none of us will survive."

units.zh: 進逵入鄂州，方攻下長山，叔嗣以兵襲武陵。
units.en: While Jinkui was inside Ezhou capturing Changshan, Shusi struck Wuling with an army.
units.literal: Jinkui entered Ezhou and was just taking Changshan when Shusi with troops raided Wuling.

units.zh: 進逵聞之，輕舟而歸，與叔嗣戰武陵城外，進逵敗，見殺。
units.en: Hearing the news, Jinkui raced back in light boats, fought Shusi outside Wuling, was defeated, and was killed.
units.literal: When Jinkui heard of it he returned in light boats, fought Shusi outside Wuling, was defeated, and was killed.

units.zh: 周行逢，武陵人也。
units.en: Zhou Xingfeng was a native of Wuling.
units.literal: Zhou Xingfeng was a native of Wuling.

units.zh: 與王進逵俱為靜江軍卒，事希萼為軍校。
units.en: He and Wang Jinkui had both served in the Jingjiang army under Xie as junior officers.
units.literal: He and Wang Jinkui were both soldiers of the Jingjiang army and served Xie as army officers.

units.zh: 進逵攻邊鎬，行逢別破益陽，殺李景兵二千餘人，擒其將李建期。
units.en: While Jinkui fought Bian Hao, Xingfeng separately took Yiyang, killed more than two thousand Southern Tang troops, and captured General Li Jianqi.
units.literal: When Jinkui attacked Bian Hao, Xingfeng on a separate route broke Yiyang, killed more than two thousand of Li Jing's troops, and captured his general Li Jianqi.

units.zh: 進逵為武安軍節度使，拜行逢集州刺史，為進逵行軍司馬。
units.en: When Jinkui became military commissioner of Wu'an, Xingfeng was named prefect of Jizhou and served as his staff marshal.
units.literal: When Jinkui became military commissioner of the Wu'an army, Xingfeng was appointed prefect of Jizhou and served as Jinkui's acting army marshal.

units.zh: 進逵與劉言有隙，行逢為畫謀策襲殺言。
units.en: When Jinkui and Liu Yan fell out, Xingfeng devised the plot that killed Yan.
units.literal: When Jinkui and Liu Yan had a rift, Xingfeng devised the stratagem for a surprise attack that killed Yan.

units.zh: 進逵據武陵，行逢據潭州。
units.en: Jinkui held Wuling while Xingfeng held Tanzhou.
units.literal: Jinkui held Wuling; Xingfeng held Tanzhou.

units.zh: 顯德元年，拜行逢武清軍節度使，權知潭州軍府事。
units.en: In the first year of Xiande (954) he was appointed military commissioner of Wuqing and given provisional control of Tanzhou headquarters.
units.literal: In the first year of Xiande he was appointed military commissioner of the Wuqing army and given provisional charge of Tanzhou military headquarters affairs.

units.zh: 潘叔嗣殺進逵，或勸其入武陵，叔嗣曰：「吾殺進逵，救死而已，武陵非吾利也。」
units.en: After Pan Shusi killed Jinkui, some urged him to seize Wuling. Shusi said, "I killed him to save myself. Wuling holds no profit for me."
units.literal: When Pan Shusi killed Jinkui, some urged him to enter Wuling; Shusi said, "I killed Jinkui only to save my life—Wuling is no advantage to me."

units.zh: 乃還岳州，遣其客將李簡率武陵人迎行逢於潭州。
units.en: He returned to Yuezhou and sent his client officer Li Jian with Wuling men to bring Xingfeng from Tanzhou.
units.literal: He then returned to Yuezhou and sent his guest general Li Jian leading men of Wuling to welcome Xingfeng at Tanzhou.

units.zh: 行逢入武陵，或請以潭州與叔嗣，行逢曰：「叔嗣殺主帥，罪當死，以其迎我，未忍殺爾。
units.en: When Xingfeng entered Wuling, some suggested giving him Tanzhou. Xingfeng said, "Shusi murdered his commander and deserved death. Because he brought me in, I spared him.
units.literal: When Xingfeng entered Wuling, some asked that Tanzhou be given to Shusi; Xingfeng said, "Shusi killed his commander-in-chief—the crime deserves death; because he welcomed me, I have not borne to kill him.

units.zh: 若與武安，是吾使之殺王公也。」
units.en: To give him Wu'an would be to commission him to kill Lord Wang."
units.literal: If I gave him Wu'an, that would be my making him kill Lord Wang."

units.zh: 召以為行軍司馬。
units.en: He summoned Shusi to serve as acting army marshal.
units.literal: He summoned him to be acting army marshal.

units.zh: 叔嗣怒，稱疾不至，行逢怒曰：「是又欲殺我矣！」
units.en: Shusi refused in anger, pleading illness. Xingfeng raged, "He plans to kill me again!"
units.literal: Shusi was angry, pleaded illness, and would not come; Xingfeng said in anger, "He means to kill me again!"

units.zh: 乃陽以武安與之，召使至府受命，至則殺之。
units.en: He pretended to offer Wu'an, summoned Shusi to headquarters to take command, and killed him on arrival.
units.literal: He then falsely offered him Wu'an, summoned him to come to headquarters to receive appointment, and when he arrived killed him.

units.zh: 行逢故武陵農家子，少貧賤無行，多慷慨大言。
units.en: Xingfeng had been a farmer's son from Wuling, poor and rough in youth, prone to grandiose talk.
units.literal: Xingfeng was formerly a farm boy of Wuling; in youth he was poor, base, and without propriety, and often spoke bold, grand words.

units.zh: 及居武陵，能儉約自勉勵，而性勇敢，果於殺戮，麾下將吏素恃功驕慢者，一以法繩之。
units.en: Once established in Wuling he lived frugally and drove himself hard. Brave and ruthless, he punished by law every officer who had grown arrogant on past merit.
units.literal: When he dwelt in Wuling he could be frugal and self-restraining; yet by nature he was brave and decisive in killing; generals and officers under him who had long relied on merit and were arrogant—all were bound by law.

units.zh: 大將十餘人謀為亂，行逢召宴諸將，酒半，以壯士擒下斬之，一境皆畏服。
units.en: When more than ten senior generals plotted mutiny, Xingfeng feasted them, and at mid-banquet had brawny men seize and behead them. The whole region submitted in fear.
units.literal: More than ten great generals plotted rebellion; Xingfeng summoned them to a banquet for the officers; when the wine was half gone, strong men seized them and beheaded them; the whole territory feared and submitted.

units.zh: 民過無大小皆死，夫人嚴氏諫曰：「人情有善惡，安得一概殺之乎！」
units.en: He executed people for offenses great and small. His wife Lady Yan protested, "People differ in guilt—how can you kill them all alike?"
units.literal: For any offense, great or small, the people died; his wife Lady Yan remonstrated, saying, "Among human feelings there is good and evil—how can one kill them all alike!"

units.zh: 行逢怒曰：「此外事，婦人何知！」
units.en: Xingfeng snapped, "That is men's business—what does a woman know!"
units.literal: Xingfeng said angrily, "This is outside affairs—what does a woman know!"

units.zh: 嚴氏不悅，紿曰：「家田佃戶，以公貴，頗不力農，多恃勢以侵民，請往視之。」
units.en: Displeased, Lady Yan pretended: "Our tenants, emboldened by your rank, neglect the fields and bully the neighbors. Let me go inspect the estate."
units.literal: Lady Yan was displeased and pretended, saying, "The tenant farmers on our family fields, because my lord is exalted, are quite slack in farming and often rely on power to encroach on the people—I ask to go and inspect."

units.zh: 至則營居以老，歲時衣青裙押佃戶送租入城。
units.en: She settled on the estate to live out her days, and each season, in a plain blue skirt, she escorted the tenants bringing rent into town.
units.literal: When she arrived she set up a dwelling to live out her old age; at the seasons she wore a blue skirt and escorted the tenant farmers delivering rent into the city.

units.zh: 行逢往就見之，勞曰：「吾貴矣，夫人何自苦邪！」
units.en: Xingfeng visited and said, "I am a great man now—why do you punish yourself so?"
units.literal: Xingfeng went to visit her and said in consolation, "I am exalted now—why does my lady torment herself!"

units.zh: 嚴氏曰：「公思作戶長時乎？
units.en: Lady Yan asked, "Do you remember when you were a village headman?
units.literal: Lady Yan said, "Does my lord recall when he was a village head?

units.zh: 民租後時，常苦鞭撲，今貴矣，宜先期以率眾，安得遂忘壟畝間乎！」
units.en: When rent was late, you were flogged. Now that you are powerful, you should pay early and set an example. How can you forget the fields?"
units.literal: When the people's rent was late, you often suffered the lash; now you are exalted—you should pay early to lead the multitude; how can you forget the furrows and fields!"

units.zh: 行逢強邀之，以群妾擁升肩輿，嚴氏卒無留意，因曰：「公用法太嚴而失人心，所以不欲留者，一旦禍起，田野間易為逃死爾。」
units.en: He forced her into a sedan surrounded by concubines, but she would not stay. She said, "Your laws are too harsh and you have lost the people's hearts. If trouble comes, the countryside is the easiest place to escape death."
units.literal: Xingfeng pressed her strongly; with a crowd of concubines they lifted her into a sedan chair; Lady Yan in the end had no wish to stay and therefore said, "My lord's use of law is too severe and loses people's hearts—that is why I do not wish to remain: once disaster rises, the open fields are easy for fleeing death."

units.zh: 行逢為少損。
units.en: Xingfeng eased his severity somewhat.
units.literal: Xingfeng moderated somewhat.

units.zh: 建隆三年，行逢病，召其將吏，以其子保權屬之曰：「吾起隴畝為團兵，同時十人，皆以誅死，惟衡州刺史張文表獨存，然常怏怏不得行軍司馬。
units.en: In the third year of Jianlong (962), Xingfeng fell ill and summoned his officers. Entrusting his son Baoquan to them, he said, "I rose from the fields as a militiaman. Of ten comrades, all were executed except Zhang Wenbiao of Hengzhou, who still broods over never receiving the post of staff marshal.
units.literal: In the third year of Jianlong, Xingfeng fell ill, summoned his generals and officers, and entrusted his son Baoquan to them, saying, "I rose from the fields as a militiaman; of ten comrades at the time, all were put to death by execution—only Zhang Wenbiao, prefect of Hengzhou, survives, yet he is often discontent at not receiving the post of acting army marshal.

units.zh: 吾死，文表必叛，當以楊師璠討之。
units.en: When I die, Wenbiao will rebel. Send Yang Shilu against him.
units.literal: When I die, Wenbiao is certain to rebel—you should use Yang Shilu to suppress him.

units.zh: 如其不能，則嬰城勿戰，自歸於朝廷。」
units.en: If he cannot prevail, hold the walls, do not fight, and surrender to the court yourself."
units.literal: If he cannot succeed, then hold the walls and do not fight, and submit of your own accord to the court."

units.zh: 行逢卒，子保權立。
units.en: Xingfeng died, and his son Baoquan succeeded him.
units.literal: Xingfeng died; his son Baoquan succeeded.

units.zh: 文表聞之，怒曰：「行逢與我起微賤而立功名，今日安能北面事小兒乎！」
units.en: When Wenbiao heard the news, he raged: "Xingfeng and I rose from nothing together. How can I bow to a child now?"
units.literal: When Wenbiao heard of it he said in anger, "Xingfeng and I rose from humble beginnings to establish merit—how today can I face north and serve a boy!"

units.zh: 遂舉兵叛，攻下潭州。
units.en: He rebelled and captured Tanzhou.
units.literal: He then raised troops in rebellion and took Tanzhou.

units.zh: 保權乞師於朝廷，亦命楊師璠討文表，告以先人之言，感激涕泣，師璠亦泣，顧其軍曰：「汝見郎君乎？
units.en: Baoquan begged the Song court for aid and was given Yang Shilu to fight Wenbiao. Reciting his father's warning, he wept with emotion. Shilu wept too and told his troops, "Have you seen our young lord?
units.literal: Baoquan begged troops from the court, which also ordered Yang Shilu to attack Wenbiao; he told them his father's words; moved, he wept; Shilu wept as well; he turned to his army and said, "Have you seen the young master?

units.zh: 年未成人而賢若此。」
units.en: Not yet a man, yet so worthy as this."
units.literal: Not yet grown to manhood, yet so worthy as this."

units.zh: 軍士奮然，皆思自效。
units.en: The troops were stirred and eager to serve.
units.literal: The soldiers were stirred and all wished to devote themselves.

units.zh: 師璠至平津亭，文表出戰，大敗之。
units.en: Shilu reached Pingjin Pavilion. Wenbiao gave battle and was routed.
units.literal: Shilu reached Pingjin Pavilion; Wenbiao came out to fight and was greatly defeated.

units.zh: 初，保權之乞師也，太祖皇帝遣慕容延釗討文表，未至而文表為師璠所執。
units.en: When Baoquan first asked for aid, Emperor Taizu sent Murong Yanjiao against Wenbiao, but before Yanjiao arrived, Shilu had already captured him.
units.literal: Earlier, when Baoquan begged for troops, the Taizu Emperor sent Murong Yanjiao to attack Wenbiao; before he arrived Wenbiao was seized by Shilu.

units.zh: 延釗兵入朗州，保權舉族朝於京師，其後事具國史。
units.en: Yanjiao's army entered Langzhou. Baoquan brought his clan to court. His later career is recorded in the dynastic histories.
units.literal: Yanjiao's troops entered Langzhou; Baoquan led his whole clan to audience at the capital; his later affairs are recorded in full in the national histories.

units.zh: 〈（殷自唐乾寧三年入湖南，至周廣順元年，凡五十七年，余具《年譜》註。）〉
units.en: (Ma Yin entered Hunan in the third year of Qianning (896) and the house endured until the first year of Guangshun (951)—fifty-seven years in all; see the "Chronological Tables" for details.)
units.literal: (From the time Yin entered Hunan in the third year of Qianning of Tang until the first year of Guangshun of Zhou, altogether fifty-seven years—the details are set forth in the "Chronological Tables" commentary.)
